concept.name: Bracket order
concept.definition: A compound order that surrounds a primary (parent) order with two opposite-side exit orders: a profit-taking limit order on one side and a protective stop order on the other. Once the parent fills, the two exits work as an OCO pair - whichever executes first cancels the other.
concept.intuition: It packages a complete trade plan in one ticket: entry, target, and stop, so the position is never left unmanaged.
concept.mechanics: A buy parent is bracketed by a high-side sell limit and a low-side sell stop (mirror image for a sell parent). The exit orders are transmitted when the parent fills; execution of either exit cancels its sibling. The whole structure is maintained by the broker's order-management system.
concept.failure_modes: The stop leg still becomes a market order when triggered, so gap moves can exit far below the intended stop price. Partial parent fills and cancel-replace races can also leave mismatched exit quantities.
concept.misconceptions: A bracket does not guarantee bounded loss - the stop leg guarantees an exit attempt, not an exit price. It is also not an exchange-native type on most venues; it is broker-side order logic.
concept.example: You buy 200 shares at $100 with a bracket: sell limit at $108 and sell stop at $96. The stock rallies to $108, the limit fills, and the $96 stop is canceled automatically.
